messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate (production) — window=5m p99=2.4s p95=0.88s QPS drop on some shards, error-rate 0.6% :warning:
amelia: seeing this in telemetry now. p99 spike started ~5467889800. looks correlated with a small prefix-key rotation we rolled ~40m ago? :thinking_face:
raj: confirmed. prefixhash v3 rollout hit ~5467862000. we saw a ~30% cache-hit drop on kv-prefix across regions eu-west-1 & us-east-1. latency correlates with low hit-rate on hot shards.
marta: any active customer alerts? I'm drafting a note but need impact numbers first.
jing: pulled tail logs from streamers. sample error trace: `KVCacheMiss -> fallback fetch -> serialize -> finish` ; fallback fetch adds ~600-700ms when miss rate spikes. some requests hit fallback twice due to retry window.
amelia: interesting — miss distribution looks uneven. shard-group A (sg-a) p99=3.1s, sg-b p99=1.1s. heatmap attached (link): https://redwood.internal/graph/5467890123/hitmap — low entropy keys concentrated on a handful of prefixes.
raj: hypothesis: prefix rehash introduced a subtle salt change for keys created before rotation, causing effective namespace split and lower hit rates. cache metadata shows many prefixes now miss because namespace token changed.
ops-bot: DEPLOY-LOG: prefixhash-rollout:v3 -> finished rolling to 40% @5467862000 by rollout-service (canary passed). No automated rollback.
marta: customer-impact calc — affected sessions ~0.9% of total traffic but concentrated customers X/Y. latency increase causing degraded streaming UX (stalls). drafting CS note.
jing: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback prefixhash to v2 (expensive op but immediate fix for hits), 2) force rekey/rehash backward-compat shim in serving layer (dev time required), 3) short term: steer traffic for high-QPS customers to fallback pool with older cache mappings.
amelia: rolling back prefixhash: ops effort + risk of new inconsistency if any data written with v3. need checklist. raj, are there any write-only clients that wrote new keys under v3?
raj: small write window during rollout ~5467862100-5467865600. but most writes are idempotent. still need careful rekey mapping and a database migration plan. not ideal for live quick fix.
evan: I can open a rapid rollback runbook but prefer traffic steering + cache warmup first. We can add a shim to map v3 tokens to v2 for reads only, but that still needs deploy.
amelia: can we do an aggressive cache pre-warm on hot prefixes? script to re-populate KV from origin for top-1000 prefixes.
ops-bot: RUN: kv-prefetcher --shard sg-a --prefix-list top1000 --concurrency 8 --dry=false started @5467890300 (eta 10m). Logs: `prefetcher: 210k keys warmed, avg fetch 45ms`
raj: triggering traffic steering: route 20% of sg-a traffic to fallback pool (with stable v2 mapping) while pre-warm runs. Command: `routerctl route set /streaming sg-a fallback-pool --pct 20`
amelia: done — I ran routerctl and confirmed via router metrics that 20% is diverted. monitoring p99 for sg-a now.
ops-bot: ROUTER: route change applied by amelia @5467890405 — 20% traffic -> fallback-pool.
jing: early numbers: sg-a p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.9s after steering and prewarm started. p95 steady ~0.6s. error-rate trending down.
marta: putting a short customer-facing note in #customer-impact: "We are investigating increased streaming latency; mitigation work underway and some traffic has been routed to a fallback to reduce stall events. We'll update in 30m."
raj: heads-up: if fallback-pool warms up, we should be cautious about double-writes or cache divergence. ensure fallbacks are read-only caches behind origin.
evan: I'll take this to mitigation lead. creating a remediation ticket and will coordinate rollback if needed. Assigning to me and amelia.
amelia: timeline: +2m monitor, +10m pre-warm finish, +30m decision to rollback vs full rollout pause.
ops-bot: PREFETCHER: completed @5467890900 — 1.02M keys warmed across shards. average hit-rate uplift +18% on sg-a.
jing: after pre-warm +20% steering, sg-a p99 now 1.05s, global p99 1.02s. still above target of 0.8s but much improved.
marta: CS update sent. customer replies: one customer reported degraded doc-streaming but accepted workaround for now.
raj: I'll prepare a safe rollback checklist in case rollback chosen: steps include freeze writes for 30s, run back-translate script, update rollout-service flags, validate checksums. Estimated 15-20m to rollback end-to-end.
evan: Oncall handoff plan: I'll own next 2h and ensure no regressions. amelia — please call me if p99 rises above 1.5s.
amelia: acknowledged. leaving thread for now, ping me for any escalations.
incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff recorded — evan assigned as incident lead @5467890600.
evan: taking over. current state summary (5467890700): mitigation=traffic-steering+prefetch completed, sg-a p99=1.05s, global p99=1.02s, next action: monitor for 1h and decide on rollback only if p99 >1.2s or customer impact increases.
marta: I'll stay on CS and surface any new customer complaints here.
raj: I'll keep working on rollback checklist and a read-shim proposal.
jing: saving logs and exporting trace for postmortem. recommend postmortem focus: rollout gating (canary size), key-rotation compatibility tests, prewarm automation.
evan: thanks all. closing live bridge in 30m if metrics hold. leaving final notes for postmortem owners. :white_check_mark:
